title: ADS1299 EEG device profile
description: Describes ONE physical device: one chip configuration, one board build, one firmware. Every field carries its provenance, because the failure this schema exists to prevent is a number inferred from a datasheet and never measured. Two such numbers are known to be wrong in an existing implementation; see conformance/test_chip_invariants.py.

claim.description: A value plus how it came to be believed.

provenance.description: measured = read off this hardware, with a procedure. closed-form = follows from a datasheet relation with no free parameter. declared = asserted by whoever built it, not independently checked. unverified = believed, provenance unknown -- anything depending on this field MUST refuse to run.

procedure.description: How it was measured, precisely enough to repeat. Required when provenance is 'measured'.

n.description: Sample size behind the measurement, where one applies.

chip.description: ADS1299 family behaviour. NOT configurable per board -- these follow from the part and its register settings.

lead_off_freq_divisor.description: The impedance carrier sits at sample_rate / divisor. With FLEAD_OFF=11 the ADS1299 lead-off source runs at fDR/4, so the carrier TRACKS the sample rate. It is not a fixed physical frequency that aliases -- that model breaks the moment the rate changes, and it is wrong in at least one existing implementation.

decimation_response.description: 'sinc3' -- the ADS1299 digital decimation filter, sinc^3(f/fs). Rate-independent at f/fs, which is why the carrier attenuation is the same constant at every sample rate.

board.description: Per build. Every one of these MUST be measured on the board in question -- none can be inferred from the chip.

r_series_ohm.description: Protection resistor per electrode. Trades ESD headroom against CMRR at roughly 1:1 in amplitude -- the common-mode leak scales linearly with it.

carrier_slope_uv_per_kohm.description: Slope of carrier amplitude against total path impedance.

carrier_intercept_uv.description: Additive intercept. The response is NOT through the origin. A single-point calibration forces it through zero and folds the intercept into the slope, which is measurably wrong at the far end of the impedance range. Requires a two-point resistor ladder.

cm_dm_at_50hz_db.description: Common-mode to differential conversion. Scales with r_series_ohm.

analogue_pole_hz.description: Any single-pole roll-off beyond the chip's sinc^3, in absolute frequency. Board-dependent. Null if absent, but 'absent' is itself a measurement.

firmware.description: Declared by whoever wrote the firmware, and verifiable against a known input. NOTHING here may be inferred from a register value alone.

uv_scale_factor.description: Multiply CSV values by this to get true input-referred microvolts. THE CENTRAL TRAP: this is a property of the firmware's conversion, not of the PGA register. An implementation that infers this from the PGA gain can differ materially from what a matched-sine measurement on the same board reports. Declaring it from the register is how that happens. Verify with a known differential input before trusting it.

interference_lines_hz.description: Explicit list of instrumental line frequencies in Hz. MUST NOT be derived from the sample rate. One such comb is a FIXED 25 Hz harmonic series locked to a clock, and expressing it as k*fs/20 happens to be right at one rate and wrong at every other.

channel_order.description: TRUE electrode positions in CSV column order. Header labels are not evidence -- headers have been observed listing electrode names in a different order from the physical channels. Readers must select POSITIONALLY.

conventions.description: Choices that are neither chip nor board nor firmware, but which change every reported number if two implementations disagree. They are not derivable; they must be declared.

carrier_amplitude_convention.description: How a measured carrier peak-to-peak is converted before Ohm's law. 'sine_rms' = Vpp/(2*sqrt(2)), correct when the decimation filter has removed the square wave's harmonics and the carrier arrives near-sinusoidal. 'square_rms' = Vpp/2. 'legacy_sqrt2' = Vpp/sqrt(2), a convention found in older lab scripts that is twice the sine value -- it must be declared, never inherited silently, because every impedance it produces is off by that factor.

analysis_rate_hz.description: Target rate after decimation, if the chain decimates. Must divide the source rate by an integer. A value chosen because it happens to divide two particular source rates is a property of those devices, not of the method.

epoch_seconds.description: Epoch length for rejection and spectral averaging.

epoch_gates.description: Rejection thresholds, as an object. MUST come from here or an explicit configuration -- never a literal in code (R-40.12). A threshold tuned until the output looks reasonable has been fitted to the answer and carries no independent evidence; derive them from labelled artefact recordings, or declare them as conventions and say so.
